graphEvents.label: All runtimes render the same brief from the canonical renderer
Health records exist only on the hook adapter

label: Every runtime renders the same brief string from the canonical renderAdvisorBrief, so the per-runtime byte difference for the same recommendation is zero.
No runtime truncates a live brief: the plugin caps at 80 tokens and 2048 characters against a measured 296-byte median.
The OpenCode plugin carries the same directive-dedup rule, so the 218-byte first message and the 78-byte steady state are runtime-wide.
The plugin envelope carries freshness, cacheHit, skillLabel and recommendationCount but no duration and no writer, so a plugin health record is a new subsystem not a pass-through.
The Claude hook already receives result.metrics.durationMs and cacheHit, which is why the default flip is two lines there and larger elsewhere.
Change 1 covers four of six runtimes; an OpenCode-only user still sees no hook health and the change description must say so.
